user.title: Heat Load Predictor
user.description: The defaults suit a typical house with an 8 kW heat pump. Replace them with your own figures here, or later under Configure. The README explains how to estimate each one.

data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity with an hourly forecast.
data_description.indoor_temp_entity: Sets the house's starting temperature. Without it, the model assumes the house is at its target.
data_description.heat_loss_w_per_k: Whole-house heat loss per degree of indoor-outdoor difference. A heat loss survey's design figure divided by (21 - design outdoor temperature) gives this; see the README for other ways to estimate it.
data_description.thermal_capacity_kwh_per_k: Heat stored per degree of house temperature. Sets how fast the house cools and recovers. See the README to measure it.
data_description.internal_gains_w: Average free heat from people, appliances and sun.
data_description.standby_w: Controls and circulation pump, drawn all the time.
data_description.cop_curve: COP at each outdoor temperature, as temp:COP pairs, e.g. -10:2.2, 2:2.9, 7:3.6. Use figures for your weather-compensated flow temperatures.
data_description.max_output_curve: Heat pump maximum heat output (kW) at each outdoor temperature, as temp:kW pairs.
data_description.horizon_hours: How far ahead to forecast. Limited by the weather forecast.
data_description.preheat: Start heating early so the house reaches each step up in the schedule on time.

error.bad_curve: Write the curve as temperature:value pairs separated by commas.
error.curve_positive: Curve values must be above zero.

battery.title: Battery planner
battery.description: Plans when to charge the battery in cheap windows so it covers the heat pump and house until the next one, and when to discharge overnight to make room for solar. Automations copy the plan into your inverter; see the README for a Solis example.

data.battery_reserve_soc: Arrive at each cheap window at
data.discharge_threshold_soc: Skip discharge if target is above
data.solar_headroom_kwh: Extra room to leave for solar

data_description.battery_soc_entity: A sensor reporting the battery's state of charge in %.
data_description.solar_today_entity: A sensor with a detailedForecast attribute of half-hour slots (period_start, pv_estimate in kW), as provided by the Solcast integration. Leave empty if you have no solar.
data_description.solar_tomorrow_entity: Tomorrow's equivalent, so overnight plans can see the next day's solar.
data_description.battery_min_soc: The inverter's lowest allowed SOC. Plans never go below it.
data_description.battery_reserve_soc: Each charge is sized so the battery reaches the next cheap window at this SOC. Set a few % above the minimum to absorb forecast errors.
data_description.baseload_kw: Average draw of everything except the heat pump.
data_description.export_limit_kw: Solar beyond what the house uses and this export limit has to go into the battery or be lost.
data_description.cheap_windows: Daily times, e.g. 04:00-07:00, 13:00-16:00, 22:00-00:00 (Cosy Octopus). Each window is a charge slot, numbered in this order.
data_description.discharge_windows: Daily times to empty the battery ahead of big solar days, e.g. 00:30-05:30. Leave empty to never discharge.
data_description.discharge_threshold_soc: If the room the solar needs only means discharging to above this SOC, it isn't worth it and the window is skipped.
data_description.solar_headroom_kwh: Added to the solar room calculation as a safety margin.

error.bad_curve: Write the curve as temperature:value pairs separated by commas.

error.bad_windows: Write windows as HH:MM-HH:MM separated by commas.
error.soc_required: Choose the battery state of charge sensor.
error.reserve_below_min: The arrival SOC can't be below the minimum SOC.
